stem: An urban planning study measures the commute time (minutes) for a sample of 30 city workers. The sample mean is 38.6 min with a sample standard deviation of 13.2 min. However, 2 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 28 observations have a mean of 36.6 min and standard deviation of 8.0 min. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 38.6, 95% CI = [33.7, 43.5]. Without outliers: mean = 36.6, 95% CI = [33.6, 39.6]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [33.6, 43.5]. Point estimate: 37.6 min.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [33.6, 43.5].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
